fullPassage: In 1977, psychologists Lynn Hasher and David Goldstein asked a group of college students how certain they were that sixty general-knowledge trivia-like statements were either true or false. The students were asked to evaluate the sixty statements three times, at two-week intervals. Crucially, only twenty of the statements were repeated each time; the other forty were new. The researchers then compared the 'truth-ratings' of the repeated versus non-repeated statements. What they found was astonishing. Regardless of whether the statement was true or false, belief in the truth of the claim went up as a function of repetition. In other words, the more often you hear a statement, the more 'true' it sounds. This became known as the illusory truth effect.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 전치사 of 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하므로 동사 repeat을 명사형 repetition으로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 전치사 of의 목적어 자리 → 명사 필요 → 동사 repeat → 명사 repetition(반복). a function of repetition = 반복의 함수(결과).

questions.passage: In other words, the more often you hear a statement, the more 'true' it sounds. This became known as the __________ (illusion) truth effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 명사 truth effect를 앞에서 수식하는 형용사가 필요하므로 명사 illusion을 형용사 illusory로 바꾼다.
det.analysis: 명사구 truth effect를 수식하는 자리 → 형용사 필요 → 명사 illusion → 형용사 illusory(착각의). the illusory truth effect = 착각적 진실 효과.

questions.passage: In 1977, psychologists Lynn Hasher and David Goldstein asked a group of college students how certain they were that sixty general-knowledge trivia-like statements were either true or false. The students were asked to evaluate the sixty statements three times, at two-week __________. Crucially, only twenty of the statements were repeated each time; the other forty were new. The researchers then compared the 'truth-ratings' of the repeated versus non-repeated statements. What they found was astonishing. Regardless of whether the statement was true or false, belief in the truth of the claim went up as a function of repetition. In other words, the more often you hear a statement, the more 'true' it sounds. This became known as the illusory truth effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: intervals(간격). 학생들은 진술을 2주 '간격'으로 세 번에 걸쳐 평가하도록 요청받았다.
det.analysis:
① prices(가격): 문맥 부적합

② corners(모퉁이): 문맥 부적합

③ intervals(간격) ←정답: three times, at two-week ___ (세 번, 2주 간격으로) — 시간 간격을 나타냄

④ groups(집단): 문맥 부적합

questions.passage: In 1977, psychologists Lynn Hasher and David Goldstein asked a group of college students how certain they were that sixty general-knowledge trivia-like statements were either true or false. The students were asked to evaluate the sixty statements three times, at two-week intervals. Crucially, only twenty of the statements were repeated each time; the other forty were new. The researchers then compared the 'truth-ratings' of the repeated versus non-repeated statements. What they found was astonishing. Regardless of whether the statement was true or false, belief in the truth of the claim went up as a __________ of repetition. In other words, the more often you hear a statement, the more 'true' it sounds. This became known as the illusory truth effect.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸: function(함수/작용). 믿음은 반복에 '따라(as a function of)' 커졌다 — 반복이 늘수록 믿음이 커진다는 관계.
det.analysis:
① function(함수/작용) ←정답: as a function of repetition(반복의 함수로서) — 반복에 따라 결정됨

② belief(믿음): 문맥 부적합

③ effect(효과): 문맥 부적합

④ shortage(부족): 문맥 부적합
